name: glm-5.3-flash-nvfp4-tp2
description: GLM-5.3-Flash on the RedHatAI NVFP4 checkpoint (compressed-tensors, corruption-free), TP2 across both Sparks, native MTP k=3, 262K context.

source.title: GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 (RedHatAI) — TP2 + MTP3
source.author: himorishige (settings), tonyd2wild (image), RedHatAI (checkpoint)
requirements: Weights RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 (184 GiB) on both nodes. The settings were measured with revision 18d55bfd; Pin with model ref 18d55bfd5a2194887738da73753975c9d3842f46 to use exactly that snapshot.
Image ghcr.io/tonyd2wild/vllm-glm53-flash:sm121-v11-dflash2 (Pin resolves the multi-arch digest; the first activation pulls it on both nodes).

The himorishige repo also bind-mounts sparse_attn_indexer_kpool_sm121.py (SM121 top-k fix). If loading or long decodes fail with a sparse-MLA / top-k assert, install it as a mod (`tsm mods file-patch glm53-sm121-sparse-attn --file sparse_attn_indexer_kpool_sm121.py --target /usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer_kpool.py`) and add glm53-sm121-sparse-attn to advanced.mods, as the DFlash2 recipe does.
notes: Use the RedHatAI checkpoint, not ModelOpt NVFP4 builds: those emit intermittent corrupted tokens in vLLM (#54150).
Dropping eager mode (CUDA graphs) measured +22-38% decode on RedHatAI weights (chishiki37) — try it once this profile is known-good: set advanced.eager_mode=false in a new revision.
reasoning parser deepseek_r1 is what the measured recipe uses; the upstream vLLM recipe uses glm47 — switch if your image ships it.
KV/token ≈ 7 KB (fp8, no drafter) per tonyd2wild's measurement; used by the planner.
